unit: Unit 1: Unit 1: Introduction to C & Fundamentals

questions.question: Which programming language directly served as the predecessor to C?

options.A: ALGOL 60

questions.explanation: C was developed as an evolution of Ken Thompson's B language, which derived from BCPL.

questions.question: In which year and facility was C initially created by Dennis Ritchie?

options.A: 1969 at IBM Research

questions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in 1972 during the Unix OS rewrite.

questions.question: What primary requirement drove the creation of C at Bell Labs?

options.A: Creating a database language
options.B: Rewriting the Unix operating system in a system-programming language

questions.explanation: C provided high-level control and direct low-level memory access needed to implement Unix.

questions.question: How did C improve upon its predecessor, the B language?

options.A: By adding automatic garbage collection
options.B: By introducing data typing (char, int, float) to a previously typeless language
options.D: By requiring graphical user interface syntax

questions.explanation: B was a typeless language operating on raw machine words; C introduced explicit data typing.

questions.question: Why is C characterized as a 'middle-level' programming language?

options.A: It combines high-level structured programming constructs with low-level direct memory/hardware access capabilities
options.B: It executes at half the speed of assembly
options.C: It can only run on mid-range computers
options.D: It bridges C++ and Java syntax

questions.explanation: C offers high-level control structures (loops, functions) alongside low-level memory manipulation (pointers, bitwise operations).

questions.question: Who is universally credited as the creator of C?

options.A: Dennis Ritchie

questions.explanation: Dennis M. Ritchie designed and implemented the C programming language.

questions.question: What is the foundational rule of structured programming?

options.A: Using goto statements for all jump conditions
options.B: Organizing programs using three control structures: sequence, selection, and iteration
options.C: Writing code inside a single monolithic block

questions.explanation: Structured programming relies on sequence, selection (if/switch), and iteration (loops) rather than unstructured jumps.

questions.question: Which construct is discouraged in structured programming due to creating 'spaghetti code'?

options.A: if-else

questions.explanation: Arbitrary jumps via goto destroy modular control flow and hinder program analysis.

questions.question: What design methodology breaks a complex problem into smaller modular sub-routines?

options.A: Top-down modular design

questions.explanation: Top-down decomposition breaks a system into sub-modules and functions.

questions.question: What is a major maintainability advantage of structured programming?

options.A: Eliminates the need for compilers
options.B: Makes code easier to read, test, debug, and maintain through modular, single-entry single-exit control blocks

questions.explanation: Well-defined single-entry/single-exit blocks simplify debugging and logic verification.

questions.question: How does C implement structured programming features?

options.A: Through functions, block scoping {} , and structured control flow statements (if, for, while)

questions.explanation: C natively provides block scoping, function abstraction, and structured selection/looping constructs.

questions.question: What characterizes a single-entry, single-exit control block?

options.A: A code block that enters at one point and exits at one point without unpredictable jumps
options.B: A loop that executes exactly once
options.C: A main function that accepts no parameters
options.D: A file with one line of code

questions.explanation: Single-entry single-exit structures preserve predictable execution paths.

questions.question: What is the mandatory starting phase in solving a software problem?

options.A: Writing C code immediately
options.B: Understanding and defining the problem requirements

questions.explanation: Problem analysis establishes clear inputs, constraints, and expected outputs.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of steps in software problem solving?

options.A: Problem Definition -> Algorithm Design -> Coding -> Testing & Debugging

questions.explanation: Analysis precedes design, followed by coding, then testing.

questions.question: What tool visually depicts an algorithm using standardized geometric shapes?

options.A: Pseudocode

questions.explanation: Flowcharts express algorithmic logic visually through standardized symbols.

questions.question: In a flowchart, what shape is used to represent an input/output operation?

options.A: Rectangle

questions.explanation: Parallelograms represent input (e.g. read) and output (e.g. print) operations.

questions.question: What is pseudocode?

options.A: Low-level assembly language
options.B: An informal high-level description of algorithm logic using plain language constructs
options.D: Syntax errors reported by a compiler

questions.explanation: Pseudocode articulates logic clearly without language-specific syntax constraints.

questions.question: Why is algorithm design crucial prior to writing code?

options.A: It verifies logic correctness and efficiency before language implementation
options.C: It eliminates the need for testing

questions.explanation: Design prevents logic flaws and saves development effort before coding.

questions.question: Which criterion requires an algorithm to terminate after a countable number of steps?

options.A: Infinite state

questions.explanation: Finiteness guarantees an algorithm halts eventually.

questions.question: What does the 'definiteness' requirement of an algorithm specify?

options.A: Every instruction must be unambiguous and rigorously defined
options.B: The code must be written in C
options.D: The program must run on Windows

questions.explanation: Definiteness demands clear, unambiguous steps.

questions.question: What metric measures how execution time increases relative to input size N?

options.A: Time Complexity

questions.explanation: Time complexity quantifies computational time growth.

questions.question: Which Big-O notation denotes constant time complexity regardless of input size?

options.A: O(N)

questions.explanation: O(1) signifies constant execution time.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of size N?
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the search space at each step, yielding O(\log N).

questions.question: What does Space Complexity assess in algorithm design?

options.A: The physical chip area of the CPU
options.B: The total memory required by the algorithm during execution
options.C: The width of source code lines
options.D: The size of the hard drive

questions.explanation: Space complexity measures RAM consumption as a function of input size.

questions.question: Which standard was established in 1989 as the first official ANSI standard for C?

options.A: K&R C

questions.explanation: ANSI X3.159-1989 standardized C, adopted internationally as ISO C90.

questions.question: What was the informal C specification prior to ANSI standardization?

options.A: K&R C (Kernighan & Ritchie C)

questions.explanation: K&R C refers to the 1978 specification from Kernighan & Ritchie's textbook.

questions.question: Which features were introduced in the C99 standard?

options.A: Inline functions, variable length arrays (VLAs), single-line comments //, and long long int

questions.explanation: C99 brought // comments, VLAs, inline, <stdbool.h>, and long long.

questions.question: What key capabilities did C11 introduce to the standard library and language?

options.A: Native multithreading (<threads.h>), atomics (<stdbool.h>/<stdatomic.h>), and _Generic type selections

questions.explanation: C11 added multi-threading, atomic operations, static asserts, and generic expressions.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the C17 (C18) standard revision?

options.A: To introduce major new language syntax
options.B: To address technical defects and clarify C11 specifications without adding new features

questions.explanation: C17 was a bug-fix release refining C11 specifications.

questions.question: Why is adherence to ISO C standards important for software development?

options.A: It guarantees code portability across different compilers and platforms
options.D: It makes compilers free of charge

questions.explanation: Standards preserve cross-platform source code portability.

questions.question: What is the mandatory entry point function where C program execution begins?

options.A: start()

questions.explanation: C runtime environments execute main() first.

questions.question: What does a return 0; statement in main() communicate to the operating system?

options.A: Program execution encountered an unhandled exception

questions.explanation: A return status of 0 indicates normal, successful exit.

questions.question: Which standard header file provides prototypes for printf() and scanf()?

options.A: <stdlib.h>

questions.explanation: <stdio.h> contains Standard Input/Output definitions.

questions.question: Which character marks the termination of most C statements?

options.A: Period .

questions.explanation: C uses semicolons as statement terminators.

questions.question: Is C case-sensitive regarding variable and function identifiers?

options.A: No
options.B: Yes, Count and count are distinct identifiers

questions.explanation: C treats uppercase and lowercase characters as completely distinct.

questions.question: What does portability mean in the context of C programs?

options.A: Source code can compile and run on different operating systems and CPU architectures with minimal adjustment
options.B: Executable files run on any OS without recompilation
options.C: Source code fits on a floppy disk
options.D: Code runs only on handheld devices

questions.explanation: Standard C code compiles across different architectures.

questions.question: What elements constitute C's basic source character set?

options.A: Uppercase/lowercase letters, decimal digits, graphic special symbols, and white-space characters

questions.explanation: The basic character set contains alphabets, digits, special characters, and whitespaces.

questions.question: Which escape sequence represents the null character used for string termination?
questions.explanation: � represents the null byte terminating strings.

questions.question: Which escape sequence inserts a newline in output text?
What is the escape sequence for a horizontal tab?
questions.explanation: inserts a horizontal tab spacing.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a white-space character in C lexical analysis?

options.A: Space, horizontal tab, vertical tab, newline, form feed

questions.explanation: White spaces delimit tokens during syntax parsing.

questions.question: How do you include a literal double quote inside a double-quoted string literal?
questions.explanation: Escaping with " prevents prematurely closing the string.

questions.question: Which rule dictates valid identifier creation in C?

options.A: Can start with a number
options.B: Must start with a letter (A-Z, a-z) or underscore _, followed by letters, digits, or underscores
options.D: Can match a keyword like int

questions.explanation: Identifiers begin with a letter or _, containing alphanumeric characters and underscores.

questions.question: Which identifier is syntactically valid in C?

options.A: 3d_point

questions.explanation: _max_value starts with _ and uses valid characters.

questions.question: What is a reserved keyword in C?

options.A: A predefined token with fixed syntactic meaning that cannot be used as an identifier name
options.B: A variable name declared in main

questions.explanation: Keywords (e.g., while, return) are reserved by C language syntax.

questions.question: How many reserved keywords exist in standard ANSI C89?
questions.explanation: ANSI C89 defines 32 keywords.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reserved C keyword?

options.A: sizeof

questions.explanation: printf is a library function name, not a reserved keyword.

questions.question: Why is sum value an invalid identifier?

options.A: It contains a space, breaking it into two separate tokens

questions.explanation: Spaces are token separators and cannot exist within an identifier.

questions.question: What is a variable in C?

options.A: A named memory location holding a data value that can change during execution

questions.explanation: Variables represent mutable memory locations.

questions.question: Which qualifier declares a variable whose value cannot be altered after initialization?

options.A: static

questions.explanation: const marks a variable as read-only.

questions.question: What happens when code tries to assign a new value to a const int x = 5; variable?

options.A: Value updates silently

questions.explanation: Modifying a const variable triggers a compilation error.

questions.question: Which prefix indicates an octal integer constant in C?

options.A: 0x

questions.explanation: A leading zero specifies octal radix (base 8).

questions.question: How is a hexadecimal constant written in C?

options.A: Prefix 0x or 0X

questions.explanation: 0x or 0X specifies hexadecimal radix (base 16).

questions.question: What is the key difference between #define PI 3.14 and const double PI = 3.14;?

options.A: #define is a preprocessor text macro without type checking, while const is a scope-aware type-checked variable
options.C: const cannot be used in expressions
options.D: They are identical in every way

questions.explanation: Macros replace text before parsing; const uses compiler scope and typing.

questions.question: Which data type stores a single 8-bit character in C?

options.A: int

questions.explanation: char holds character codes and occupies 1 byte.

questions.question: What does the C standard guarantee regarding size ordering of integer types?

options.A: sizeof(short) <= sizeof(int) <= sizeof(long) <= sizeof(long long)
options.C: All integer types are always 32 bits
options.D: int is strictly larger than long

questions.explanation: C specifies relative minimum size guarantees for integer types.

questions.question: Which data type provides double-precision floating point storage?

options.A: float

questions.explanation: double provides 64-bit double precision floating point.

questions.question: What is the value of sizeof(char) according to the C standard?

options.A: Exactly 1 byte

questions.explanation: sizeof(char) is explicitly defined as 1.

questions.question: What range of values can an 8-bit unsigned char store?
questions.explanation: Unsigned 8-bit byte ranges from 0 to 255.

questions.question: Which keyword qualifier prevents negative values and doubles positive capacity?

options.A: signed

questions.explanation: unsigned converts the storage representation to non-negative only.

questions.question: What is an expression in C?

options.A: A valid combination of operators, constants, and variables yielding a single computed value

questions.explanation: Expressions compute values from operands and operators.

questions.question: In val = 10 + 4 * 2;, what is val based on precedence?
questions.explanation: Multiplication evaluates before addition: 10 + (4 * 2) = 18.

questions.question: What occurs during implicit integer promotion in expressions?

options.A: Types smaller than int (e.g. char, short) are promoted to int during calculation

questions.explanation: C automatically promotes small integer types to int in expressions.

questions.question: How is explicit type casting performed in C?

options.A: (type) expression

questions.explanation: Prefixing (type) forces type conversion.

questions.question: What is the result of integer division 9 / 2 in C?
questions.explanation: Integer division truncates fractional parts to integer 4.

questions.question: How can floating-point division yielding 4.5 be evaluated from integer variables a=9 and b=2?

options.A: (float)a / b

questions.explanation: Casting one operand to float promotes division to floating point.

questions.question: What defines a compound statement or block in C?

options.A: Statements grouped within curly braces {}

questions.explanation: Curly braces {} combine multiple statements into a compound block.

questions.question: What is a null statement in C?

options.A: A standalone semicolon ; performing no operation

questions.explanation: A lonely semicolon ; forms a null statement.

questions.question: Which statement category dictates control flow execution paths?

options.A: Control statements (selection, loop, jump)

questions.explanation: Control statements direct program execution branching and repetition.

questions.question: How does an expression become an expression statement?

options.A: By appending a semicolon ;

questions.explanation: Adding a semicolon turns an expression into a complete statement.

questions.question: Where can local variable declarations be placed inside a block in C99?

options.A: Anywhere inside the block prior to usage
options.B: Strictly at line 1 of the block

questions.explanation: C99 allows mixed variable declarations and statements.

questions.question: What is the logical flaw in if (x == 0); { printf("Zero"); }?

options.A: The semicolon after if creates a null body, making the print block execute unconditionally

questions.explanation: The premature semicolon satisfies the if with an empty statement.

subtopics.title: 1.13 Compilation and Execution of C Programs

questions.question: What is the proper sequential order of C translation pipeline tools?

options.A: Preprocessor -> Compiler -> Assembler -> Linker

questions.explanation: Source passes through Preprocessor, Compiler, Assembler, then Linker.

questions.question: What action does the Preprocessor perform on source code?

options.A: Macro expansion (#define), file inclusion (#include), and comment removal

questions.explanation: The preprocessor prepares modified source text before syntax compilation.

questions.question: What file output is generated by compilation/assembly before linking?

options.A: Object file (.o / .obj)

questions.explanation: Compiling source produces relocatable object files.

questions.question: What is the responsibility of the Linker?

options.A: Combining object code files and library code into a single executable binary

questions.explanation: The linker resolves function calls across object files and libraries.

questions.question: What type of error prevents source code from successfully compiling into object code?

options.A: Compile-time (syntax) error

questions.explanation: Syntax errors violate grammar rules and stop compilation.

questions.question: An exception occurring while a program runs (e.g. segmentation fault or division by zero) is known as what?

options.A: Runtime error

questions.explanation: Errors during execution are runtime errors.

unit: Unit 2: Unit 2: Operators, Input/Output and Decision Making

questions.question: Which binary arithmetic operator calculates the remainder of integer division in C?
questions.explanation: The modulus operator % returns the remainder when two integers are divided.

questions.question: What happens if you attempt to use the modulus operator % with floating-point operands (5.5 % 2.0) in C?

options.A: Returns 1.5
options.B: Compiler error (operands must be integer types)

questions.explanation: The C % operator strictly requires integer operands. For floating-point remainder, fmod() from <math.h> must be used.

questions.question: What is the evaluated result of 15 / 6 in C?
questions.explanation: Both operands are integers, so integer division truncates to 2.

questions.question: What is the evaluated value of 15 % 6?
questions.explanation: 15 = (6 	imes 2) + 3, so remainder is 3.

questions.question: What is the result of the expression -17 % 5 in standard C99?
questions.explanation: In C99, integer division truncates toward zero, making the sign of remainder match the dividend (-17), yielding -2.

questions.question: Among arithmetic operators +, -, *, /, %, which pair has higher operator precedence?

options.A: + and -

questions.explanation: Multiplicative operators (*, /, %) have higher precedence than additive operators (+, -).

questions.question: What is the distinction between prefix increment (++x) and postfix increment (x++) in an assignment y = ++x; vs y = x++;?

options.A: Prefix increments x before evaluating its value for y; postfix evaluates x for y before incrementing x
options.D: Postfix works only on global variables

questions.explanation: ++x increments then yields value; x++ yields current value then increments.

questions.question: If x = 5;, what are the values of a and x after executing a = x++;?
questions.explanation: a gets current value 5, then x increments to 6.

questions.question: If x = 5;, what are the values of b and x after executing b = ++x;?
questions.explanation: x increments first to 6, then b is assigned 6.

questions.question: Which operator returns the memory size (in bytes) of a variable or data type?

options.A: sizeof

questions.explanation: The unary sizeof operator yields storage size in bytes.

questions.question: What does the unary address-of operator & yield when applied to variable x?

options.A: The value stored in x
options.B: The physical RAM memory address of x

questions.explanation: &x evaluates to the memory address of x.

questions.question: What does the unary indirection (dereference) operator * do when applied to pointer p (*p)?

options.A: Multiplies p by 2
options.B: Accesses the data value stored at the memory location pointed to by p

questions.explanation: Dereferencing *p retrieves or modifies the value at address p.

questions.question: What value is returned by a relational expression in C when the condition evaluates to true?

options.A: true keyword

questions.explanation: Relational comparison expressions yield integer 1 for true and 0 for false.

questions.question: Which operator tests for strict equality between two values in C?
questions.explanation: == is the relational equality operator; = is assignment.

questions.question: Which operator tests for inequality (not equal) in C?
questions.explanation: != checks if two values are not equal.

questions.question: How is the expression 10 <= 10 evaluated in C?

options.A: Evaluates to 1 (true)

questions.explanation: 10 is less than or equal to 10, so condition is true (1).

questions.question: What common logical bug occurs when writing if (x = 5) instead of if (x == 5)?

options.A: It assigns 5 to x and evaluates the expression as true (5), ignoring comparison

questions.explanation: x = 5 assigns 5 to x and yields 5 (non-zero/true), causing unintended execution.

questions.question: What is the evaluated result of chained relational comparison 5 < x < 10 when x = 2 in C?

options.A: Evaluates to false (0)
options.B: Evaluates to true (1) because (5 < 2) gives 0, and 0 < 10 gives 1

questions.explanation: Left-to-right evaluation computes (5 < 2) -> 0, then 0 < 10 -> 1 (true), proving why chained comparisons must use && instead!

questions.question: Which symbol represents the logical AND operator in C?
questions.explanation: && is logical AND; single & is bitwise AND.

questions.question: Which symbol represents the logical OR operator in C?
questions.explanation: || is logical OR; single | is bitwise OR.

questions.question: What is short-circuit evaluation in logical expressions A && B or A || B?

options.A: The compiler stops evaluating B if the outcome is fully determined by A alone

questions.explanation: For A && B, if A is false, B is not evaluated. For A || B, if A is true, B is skipped.

questions.question: Given int x = 0; if (x != 0 && (10 / x > 2)), will a divide-by-zero runtime error occur?

options.A: Yes, 10 / x executes first
options.B: No, short-circuit evaluation skips (10 / x > 2) because x != 0 evaluates to false (0)

questions.explanation: x != 0 is false, so && short-circuits and avoids evaluating 10 / 0.

questions.question: What does the unary logical NOT operator ! do to a truth value in C?

options.A: Inverts non-zero (true) to 0, and 0 (false) to 1

questions.explanation: ! logically negates truth values.

questions.question: What is the evaluated result of !(5 > 2) || (3 == 3) in C?
Which statement correctly demonstrates compound assignment operator shorthand?
questions.explanation: x += 5 compresses x = x + 5.

questions.question: What is the final value of a after int a = 10; a *= 3 + 2;?
questions.explanation: Right-hand side evaluates first: 3 + 2 = 5. Then a = a * 5 -> 10 * 5 = 50.

questions.question: Which assignment operator performs bitwise XOR and assignment in one step?
questions.explanation: ^= performs bitwise XOR assignment.

questions.question: What does multiple assignment chaining like a = b = c = 20; do in C?

options.A: Assigns 20 to c, then b, then a due to right-to-left associativity of =

questions.explanation: Assignment operators associate right-to-left.

questions.question: What is the value of x after executing int x = 16; x >>= 2;?
questions.explanation: Right shift by 2 divides integer by 2^2 = 4: 16 / 4 = 4.

questions.question: Why is the left side of an assignment operator required to be an lvalue?

options.A: An lvalue represents a modifiable memory location that can store a value

questions.explanation: Assignment target must be an lvalue (locator value / modifiable storage).

questions.question: Which operator in C is the only ternary operator (taking three operands)?

options.A: if-else

questions.explanation: condition ? expr1 : expr2 is C's sole ternary operator.

questions.question: In max = (a > b) ? a : b;, which value is assigned to max if a = 7 and b = 12?
questions.explanation: 7 > 12 is false, so second expression b (12) is evaluated and returned.

questions.question: What is a major advantage of the conditional operator over if-else statements?

options.A: It can be used inline within expressions, variable initializations, and return statements

questions.explanation: Conditional operator yields a value inline inside expressions.

questions.question: What is the evaluated output of printf("%s", (x % 2 == 0) ? "Even" : "Odd"); when x = 4?

options.A: "Even"

questions.explanation: 4 % 2 == 0 is true, choosing string literal "Even".

questions.question: What restriction applies to the result types of expr1 and expr2 in cond ? expr1 : expr2?

options.A: They must be compatible types or convertible to a common type

questions.explanation: The compiler determines a common result type for both branches.

questions.question: What is the evaluated result of nested conditional expression int status = (score >= 90) ? 1 : (score >= 50) ? 2 : 3; when score = 75?
questions.explanation: 75 >= 90 is false -> evaluates (75 >= 50) ? 2 : 3 -> 75 >= 50 is true -> yields 2.

questions.question: Which standard header file contains mathematical functions like sqrt(), pow(), sin(), and cos()?

options.A: <stdlib.h>

questions.explanation: <math.h> provides mathematical function prototypes.

questions.question: Which standard library function converts a string representation of numbers into an integer?

options.A: atoi()

questions.explanation: atoi() (ASCII to Integer) declared in <stdlib.h> converts string to int.

questions.question: Which function in <stdlib.h> terminates program execution immediately and returns a status code to OS?

options.A: abort()

questions.explanation: exit(status) flushes I/O buffers, closes files, and terminates the process.

questions.question: Which header file defines character classification and conversion utilities like isalpha(), isdigit(), toupper()?

options.A: <string.h>

questions.explanation: <ctype.h> provides character testing/conversion routines.

questions.question: What does the function rand() declared in <stdlib.h> generate?

options.A: A pseudo-random integer between 0 and RAND_MAX

questions.explanation: rand() produces pseudo-random numbers in range 0 to RAND_MAX.

questions.question: Which function seeds the pseudo-random number generator used by rand()?

options.A: srand()

questions.explanation: srand(seed) initializes the PRNG seed.

subtopics.title: 2.8 Data Input and Output: getchar() and putchar()

questions.question: What character input operation is performed by getchar() from standard input?

options.A: Reads a single character from stdin and returns its ASCII value as an int
options.B: Reads an entire line into string

questions.explanation: getchar() reads one character from stdin and returns int (to accommodate EOF).

questions.question: Why is the return type of getchar() declared as int rather than char?

options.A: To allow returning the special negative macro integer EOF upon end-of-file or error
options.B: Because C has no char type

questions.explanation: EOF is a negative integer (typically -1) outside valid unsigned char range.

questions.question: What does putchar(c) do in C?

options.A: Writes character c to standard output stdout

questions.explanation: putchar(ch) outputs character ch to stdout.

questions.question: What special macro value does getchar() return when reading reaches End-Of-File?

options.A: NULL

questions.explanation: getchar() returns macro EOF on end-of-file.

questions.question: In keyboard input loops, what causes getchar() to actually receive buffered characters on standard terminals?

options.A: Pressing the Enter key (

questions.explanation: Standard stdin is line-buffered, releasing input when newline is entered.

questions.question: Which expression reads characters continuously in a loop until end-of-file?

options.A: while ((ch = getchar()) != EOF)

questions.explanation: Assigning and checking (ch = getchar()) != EOF is standard character processing loop construct.

questions.question: In scanf("%d", &num);, why is the address-of operator & required before num?

options.A: scanf() requires a memory address pointer to store the user input into num

questions.explanation: C passes arguments by value; scanf needs the address to write input back into variable storage.

questions.question: Which format specifier is used in printf() / scanf() for an integer, float, double, and string respectively?

options.A: %d, %f, %lf, %s

questions.explanation: %d = int, %f = float, %lf = double (in scanf), %s = string.

questions.question: What value is returned by the printf() function upon execution?

options.A: The total number of characters successfully printed
options.C: The memory address of output buffer

questions.explanation: printf() returns the count of written characters (or negative code on error).

questions.question: What value is returned by scanf("%d %d", &a, &b) if input reading succeeds for both variables?

options.A: 2 (number of input items successfully matched and assigned)

questions.explanation: scanf() returns the number of successfully scanned and assigned input items.

questions.question: What format specifier modifier formats a floating point to display exactly 2 decimal places in printf()?
questions.explanation: %.2f specifies a precision of 2 decimal places.

questions.question: Why does scanf("%s", str); not require & before string array variable str?

options.A: An array name in C automatically decays into a pointer to its first element

questions.explanation: The array identifier str evaluates directly to address &str[0].

subtopics.title: 2.10 Decision Making: if, if-else, Nested if-else

questions.question: In C, how does an if statement evaluate its conditional expression?

options.A: Any non-zero expression evaluates as true; zero evaluates as false
options.B: Strictly 1 is true, everything else is false

questions.explanation: In C control structures, 0 is false and any non-zero value is true.

questions.question: What problem arises when an else clause lacks explicit block braces in nested code?

options.A: Dangling else problem (an else binds to the nearest preceding un-closed if)

questions.explanation: An else automatically attaches to the closest unclosed if unless explicit {} braces specify otherwise.

questions.question: In if (a > 5) if (b > 10) x = 1; else x = 2;, which if statement does the else belong to?

options.A: The inner if (b > 10)

questions.explanation: C grammar rules attach else to the nearest preceding if (if (b > 10)).

questions.question: What happens if no condition evaluates to true in an if ... else if ... else chain?

options.A: The fallback else block executes

questions.explanation: When all previous conditions fail, execution falls through to the optional else block.

questions.question: How many statements are executed under if (cond) statement1; statement2; when cond is false?

options.A: statement1 is skipped; statement2 executes because it lies outside the if body

questions.explanation: Without {} braces, only statement1 is guarded by if. statement2 runs sequentially.

questions.question: What is the result of if (-5) printf("A"); else printf("B");?

options.A: Prints "A" because -5 is non-zero (true)

questions.explanation: -5 is non-zero, evaluating as logically true.

questions.question: What types of expressions are permitted inside a switch(expression) selector in C?

options.A: Integral types only (int, char, enum)

questions.explanation: C switch statements evaluate integral expressions (int, char, enum). Floats/strings are prohibited.

questions.question: What happens if a break; statement is omitted at the end of a case block in a switch?

options.A: Execution 'falls through' into the subsequent case statements unconditionally

questions.explanation: Without break, execution continues sequentially into downstream case blocks (fall-through behavior).

questions.question: What is the purpose of the default: label in a switch statement?

options.A: Executes when no case constants match the selector expression
options.C: Must be placed as line 1 of switch

questions.explanation: The optional default branch executes if no case label matches.

questions.question: Must case labels in a switch statement be constant expressions known at compile time?

options.A: Yes, case expressions must evaluate to unique compile-time integer constants
options.B: No, variables are allowed in case labels

questions.explanation: case values must be unique integral constant expressions.

questions.question: Can two case labels in the same switch block share the identical constant value (case 5: and case 5:)?

options.A: No, duplicate case values trigger a compiler error

questions.explanation: Duplicate case values are illegal in a switch construct.

questions.question: Given int x = 2; switch(x) { case 1: p("1"); case 2: p("2"); case 3: p("3"); break; }, what is printed?
questions.explanation: Matches case 2:, prints "2", then falls through to case 3:, prints "3", then hits break;.

questions.question: What distinguishes an entry-controlled loop (while, for) from an exit-controlled loop (do-while)?

options.A: Entry-controlled loops check condition before body execution; exit-controlled loops execute body at least once before checking condition

questions.explanation: do-while checks condition at the bottom, guaranteeing at least 1 body execution.

questions.question: How many times will int i = 10; do { i++; } while (i < 5); execute its loop body?

options.A: Exactly 1 time

questions.explanation: The body runs once (i becomes 11), then condition 11 < 5 evaluates to false.

questions.question: What are the three expressions inside a standard for(expr1; expr2; expr3) loop header?

options.A: Initialization, condition check, and iteration update

questions.explanation: for(initialization; test_condition; iteration_step).

questions.question: What happens if the test condition expression is omitted in for(;;)?

options.A: It creates an intentional infinite loop (condition treated as permanently true)

questions.explanation: An empty test condition in a for loop defaults to true (1).

questions.question: Which loop structure is preferred when the exact number of iterations is known prior to loop entry?

options.A: for loop

questions.explanation: for loops combine counter init, bound testing, and stepping compactly.

questions.question: Given for (int i = 0; i < 5; i += 2), what values will i hold inside loop body iterations?
questions.explanation: Iteration 1: i=0, iteration 2: i=2, iteration 3: i=4. Next increment i=6 fails 6 < 5.

questions.question: What does a break; statement do inside a loop (for, while, do-while)?

options.A: Immediately terminates the innermost enclosing loop and jumps to the statement following the loop
options.B: Skips remaining statements in current iteration and restarts next iteration

questions.explanation: break exits the enclosing loop or switch construct immediately.

questions.question: What does a continue; statement do when encountered inside a loop body?

options.A: Skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and jumps directly to the loop condition test/update step

questions.explanation: continue bypasses the rest of current loop iteration.

questions.question: What does a goto label; statement perform in C?

options.A: Performs an unconditional jump to the specified statement label within the same function scope
options.B: Jumps to a function in another file

questions.explanation: goto jumps unconditionally to a function-scoped label.

questions.question: Inside a nested for loop (outer and inner), what happens when break; executes inside the inner loop?

options.A: Only the inner loop is terminated; the outer loop continues running
options.B: Both outer and inner loops terminate

questions.explanation: break terminates only the innermost loop in which it sits.

questions.question: How is a statement label defined in C for a goto target?

options.A: label_name: (identifier followed by colon)

questions.explanation: Target labels take form label_name: followed by a statement.

questions.question: When is the use of goto acceptable in professional C programming?

options.A: For cleanly jumping out of deeply nested loops to a unified error cleanup section within a function

questions.explanation: Bailing out of deeply nested structures to cleanup handlers is a common C pattern for goto.

questions.question: What is the operator precedence level of the comma operator , in C?

options.A: Lowest precedence of all C operators

questions.explanation: The comma operator , has the absolute lowest precedence in C.

questions.question: How does the comma operator expr1 , expr2 evaluate its operands and return a result?

options.A: Evaluates expr1 first, discards its result, then evaluates expr2 and returns expr2's value
options.B: Evaluates both in parallel and returns sum

questions.explanation: Comma operator evaluates left-to-right, discarding left expression result and returning right expression result.

questions.question: What is the evaluated value of int x = (3 + 2, 5 * 4);?
questions.explanation: 3 + 2 = 5 is evaluated and discarded; 5 * 4 = 20 is evaluated and assigned to x.

questions.question: Where is the comma operator most commonly utilized in C syntax?

options.A: Inside for loop header initialization and update clauses, e.g. for (i = 0, j = 10; i < j; i++, j--)

questions.explanation: In for headers, commas allow updating multiple loop variables in a single clause.

questions.question: In function arguments func(a, b), is the comma separating a and b a comma operator?

options.A: No, it is a syntax argument separator, not the comma operator
options.B: Yes, it evaluates right to left

questions.explanation: Function call commas are argument separators. To use comma operator inside argument, parentheses are required func((a, b)).

questions.question: What is the evaluated value of a after int a; a = 1, 2, 3;?

options.A: 1 (because = has higher precedence than ,, doing (a = 1), 2, 3)

questions.explanation: = binds tighter than ,, so a = 1 evaluates first. 2 and 3 evaluate as side-effect expressions!

questions.question: What is the fundamental goal of software debugging?

options.A: Identifying, isolating, and fixing defects or bugs in source code logic/execution

questions.explanation: Debugging detects and resolves bugs to ensure correct execution.

questions.question: Which basic technique involves inserting temporary printf() statements to track variable state and control flow during runtime?

options.A: Print debugging (tracing)

questions.explanation: Tracing variable state via printf is classic print-debugging.

questions.question: What is a breakpoint in an interactive debugger tool like GDB?

options.A: A designated line where debugger pauses program execution to allow inspection of variables and memory state

questions.explanation: Breakpoints halt execution so developers can inspect program registers and RAM.

questions.question: Which standard macro declared in <assert.h> tests a logical condition and aborts execution if false?

options.A: assert(condition)

questions.explanation: assert(expr) prints an error message and aborts if expr evaluates to 0.

questions.question: How can all assert() macro calls be disabled in a release compilation build without editing source code?

options.A: Defining macro #define NDEBUG before including <assert.h>

questions.explanation: NDEBUG macro turns all assert() tests into empty no-ops for release builds.

questions.question: Which tool or compiler flag is widely used to detect memory leaks, uninitialized reads, and buffer overflows in C programs?

options.A: Valgrind / AddressSanitizer (-fsanitize=address)

questions.explanation: Valgrind and ASan diagnose runtime memory access violations and dynamic memory leaks.

unit: Unit 3: Unit 3: Arrays, Strings and Pointers

questions.question: What is an array in C?

options.A: A contiguous block of memory holding a fixed number of elements of the same data type
options.B: A dynamic list of heterogeneous data types
options.C: A file on disk containing strings
options.D: A function that returns multiple integers

questions.explanation: Arrays store homogeneous data elements sequentially in contiguous memory locations.

questions.question: What is the starting index (subscript) of the first element in any C array?
questions.explanation: C uses zero-based indexing; the initial element sits at index 0.

questions.question: If an array is declared as int arr[10];, what is the index of the last valid element?
questions.explanation: For size N=10, valid indices range from 0 to N-1 = 9.

questions.question: What happens if a program reads or writes to index arr[15] on an array declared as int arr[10];?

options.A: Out-of-bounds array access causing undefined behavior (or segmentation fault)

questions.explanation: C does not perform runtime array bounds checking; out-of-bounds access is undefined behavior.

questions.question: How is the total byte size of an array int arr[20]; computed using sizeof on a system where sizeof(int) == 4?

options.A: 20 bytes

questions.explanation: Total size = element count 	imes element byte size = 20 	imes 4 = 80 bytes.

questions.question: How can the element count of an array arr be dynamically computed at compile time?

options.A: sizeof(arr) / sizeof(arr[0])

questions.explanation: Dividing total array bytes by single element bytes yields total element count.

questions.question: Which declaration syntax correctly instantiates and initializes a 1D integer array in C?
questions.explanation: Array initializer lists use curly braces {}.

questions.question: If a 1D array of size 5 is partially initialized as int arr[5] = {1, 2};, what values do the remaining elements arr[2], arr[3], arr[4] hold?

options.A: Garbage values

questions.explanation: When an initializer list is partially provided, all unmentioned elements are auto-initialized to 0.

questions.question: What happens if an uninitialized local array int arr[5]; is declared inside a function?

options.A: All elements hold unpredictable garbage values

questions.explanation: Uninitialized local automatic variables contain whatever random garbage bytes existed in stack memory.

questions.question: How do you traverse and process every element in a 1D array arr of size N?

options.A: Using a loop from i = 0 to i < N accessing arr[i]

questions.explanation: Iterating an index variable i from 0 to N-1 visits every array element sequentially.

questions.question: What happens if you omit the size dimension in an initialized array int arr[] = {4, 8, 12};?

options.A: Compiler infers size dimension automatically from initializer count (size 3)

questions.explanation: Omitting size in an initialized array lets the compiler count elements.

questions.question: When a 1D array is passed to a function void process(int a[], int n), how is the array passed?

options.A: By value (copies entire array)
options.B: By reference/pointer (passes address of first element &a[0])

questions.explanation: Arrays decay into pointers when passed to functions; changes inside function modify original array.

questions.question: How is a 2D matrix array with 3 rows and 4 columns declared in C?

options.A: int matrix[3][4];

questions.explanation: 2D array syntax uses square brackets for each dimension [rows][cols].

questions.question: In C, how are elements of a 2D array arranged in physical RAM memory?

options.A: Row-major order (row after row sequentially)

questions.explanation: C stores 2D arrays in row-major order: all elements of row 0, then row 1, etc.

questions.question: How do you access the element at row index 2 and column index 1 of int grid[3][4]?

options.A: grid[2][1]

questions.explanation: Individual element access uses [row][col] indexing.

questions.question: When declaring a 2D array parameter in a function header void display(int arr[][4], int rows), why is column dimension mandatory?

options.A: To allow compiler to calculate memory offset arithmetic row * cols + col for elements

questions.explanation: The compiler needs column size to calculate element offset addresses in row-major memory.

questions.question: What is the total number of integer elements in int data[5][10]?

options.A: 50 elements (5 	imes 10)

questions.explanation: Total elements = rows 	imes cols = 5 	imes 10 = 50.

questions.question: How is a 2D array initialized cleanly using nested braces?
questions.explanation: Nested initializer lists { {row0}, {row1} } explicitly map rows.

questions.question: What distinguishes a general character array from a formal C string?

options.A: A formal C string is a character array terminated by a null byte �

questions.explanation: A string is a null-terminated character array.

questions.question: How many bytes of storage are required to store string literal "Hello" in a character array?

options.A: 5 bytes

questions.explanation: String literals include implicit terminating � byte.

questions.question: What happens if a character array char str[5] = "Hello"; is declared without space for �?

options.A: The array lacks null-termination, causing string operations (printf("%s"), strlen) to read past array bounds

questions.explanation: Without �, string routines scan out-of-bounds until encountering a random 0 byte.

questions.question: Which expression initializes a character array with explicit null termination?
questions.explanation: Explicit element lists require manual inclusion of �.

questions.question: What format specifier prints a single character vs a null-terminated character array in printf()?

options.A: %c for single char, %s for string array
options.B: %s for single char, %d for string array
options.C: %ch for single char, %str for string array

questions.explanation: %c expects char value; %s expects pointer to null-terminated char array.

questions.question: Can you assign a new string literal directly using assignment operator str = "New"; to an existing character array char str[10]; after declaration?

options.A: No, array names are non-assignable lvalues; strcpy() must be used

questions.explanation: Array names cannot be reassigned; string copying requires strcpy() or pointer assignment.

questions.question: How are string literals defined in C source code?

options.A: Enclosed in double quotes "Like this"

questions.explanation: Double quotes define string literals; single quotes define single character constants.

questions.question: What is the memory storage duration and mutability of a string literal char *ptr = "Read Only";?

options.A: Stored in read-only data segment; modifying it via ptr[0] = 'W' causes undefined behavior (segmentation fault)
options.B: Stored on stack and fully mutable

questions.explanation: String literals are stored in read-only memory; modifying them is undefined.

questions.question: What is the difference between char a[] = "Test"; and char *p = "Test";?

options.A: a[] creates a mutable array on stack initialized with string contents; p points directly to read-only string literal memory

questions.explanation: Array initialization copies literal characters onto mutable stack memory.

questions.question: What is an empty string literal "" in C?

options.A: A string containing only a single null character � at index 0

questions.explanation: "" contains 1 byte: �.

questions.question: How does C concatenate adjacent string literals written in source code like "Hello " "World"?

options.A: The compiler automatically merges them into a single string literal "Hello World" during compilation

questions.explanation: Adjacent string literals are joined during preprocessor/translation phases.

questions.question: What does sizeof("Hello") return vs strlen("Hello")?

options.A: sizeof returns 6 (includes �); strlen returns 5 (excludes �)

questions.explanation: sizeof measures buffer memory size (6); strlen counts characters up to � (5).

questions.question: Which string initialization syntax is valid in C?

options.A: char str[] = "Welcome";

questions.explanation: char str[] = "Welcome"; lets compiler allocate 8 bytes (7 letters + �).

questions.question: If char str[10] = "Hi"; is declared, what are contents of str[0] through str[3]?
questions.explanation: Partial initialization fills H, i, �, and zeroes out all remaining bytes.

questions.question: Why is char s[3] = "Cat"; problematic in C?

options.A: Buffer holds 'C','a','t' with no room for �, resulting in non-null-terminated character array

questions.explanation: Needs 4 bytes ('C','a','t','�'). 3 bytes omits �.

questions.question: Can a string array be initialized using designated initializers in C99, e.g. char s[5] = {[0]='A', [1]='B', [2]='�'};?

options.A: Yes, C99 designated initializers allow specifying element index assignments

questions.explanation: Designated initializers permit explicit index initialization.

questions.question: What happens if a string pointer is initialized as char *s = NULL; and passed to strcpy(s, "Data");?

options.A: Segmentation fault / crash (dereferencing NULL pointer)

questions.explanation: Writing to NULL pointer address triggers a fatal segmentation fault.

questions.question: How can a character array char buf[20]; be zeroed/cleared completely upon declaration?

options.A: char buf[20] = {0}; or char buf[20] = "";

questions.explanation: {0} or "" zeroes all array elements.

questions.question: Why is scanf("%s", buffer); unsafe for reading user input strings?

options.A: It lacks buffer length checking, risking buffer overflow, and stops reading at whitespace

questions.explanation: scanf("%s") reads arbitrarily long words until whitespace, risking stack smash overflow.

questions.question: Which standard library function is safer for reading an entire input line containing spaces into string buf?

options.A: fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), stdin)

questions.explanation: fgets() enforces maximum character length limit, preventing buffer overflow.

questions.question: Why was the ISO C standard function gets() officially deprecated in C99 and removed in C11?

options.A: Inherently unsafe due to impossibility of preventing buffer overflow attacks

questions.explanation: gets() has no length parameter, causing major security vulnerabilities.

questions.question: What does puts(str); do when outputting string str to standard output?

options.A: Writes str to console and automatically appends a trailing newline

questions.explanation: puts() prints string and appends

questions.question: How does fgets(str, size, stdin) handle trailing newline characters typed by user?

options.A: If space permits, fgets() includes the

questions.explanation: fgets retains newline in buffer if input fits.

questions.question: How can scanf() be constrained to prevent reading more than 19 characters into char buf[20]?

options.A: scanf("%19s", buf);

questions.explanation: Field width specifier %19s limits read to 19 chars, saving 1 byte for �.

questions.question: Which header file must be included to use functions like strlen(), strcpy(), strcat(), and strcmp()?

options.A: <string.h>

questions.explanation: <string.h> declares standard string manipulation functions.

questions.question: What value is returned by strlen("Programming")?
questions.explanation: strlen counts characters up to (excluding) �. "Programming" has 11 letters.

questions.question: What does strcmp(str1, str2) return if str1 is lexicographically equal to str2?
questions.explanation: strcmp returns 0 if strings match identically.

questions.question: Which function appends string src onto the end of destination string dest?

options.A: strcat(dest, src)

questions.explanation: strcat concatenates source string onto destination.

questions.question: What does strstr(haystack, needle) perform?

options.A: Finds first occurrence of substring needle inside string haystack and returns pointer to it

questions.explanation: strstr locates substring match, returning pointer to first match or NULL.

questions.question: Why are strncpy(), strncat(), strncmp() bounded variants preferred over strcpy(), strcat(), strcmp()?

options.A: They accept a maximum count parameter N to prevent buffer overflow vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: The bounded strn* functions limit operations to N bytes to protect memory.

questions.question: What is a pointer variable in C?

options.A: A variable that holds the memory address of another variable
options.B: A variable that holds floating point values

questions.explanation: Pointers store memory addresses.

questions.question: Which operator symbol is used in variable declarations to specify a pointer type, e.g. int *ptr;?

options.A: * (Asterisk)

questions.explanation: * designates pointer declaration or dereference operator.

questions.question: If int x = 10; int *p = &x;, what does the expression *p evaluate to?

options.A: 10 (the value stored in x)

questions.explanation: Dereferencing *p accesses the value held at target address x.

questions.question: What is a NULL pointer in C?

options.A: A pointer assigned value NULL (typically address 0), indicating it points to no valid memory object
options.B: An uninitialized pointer containing garbage address

questions.explanation: NULL represents a reserved invalid pointer constant.

questions.question: What is a 'dangling pointer'?

options.A: A pointer holding the address of memory that has been freed/deallocated
options.C: A pointer to static global variable

questions.explanation: Dangling pointers reference invalid, deallocated memory locations.

questions.question: On a 64-bit CPU architecture, what is the byte size of any pointer (int*, char*, double*)?

options.A: 8 bytes (64 bits)
options.C: Depends on target data type size

questions.explanation: Pointer byte size depends on system address bus width (8 bytes on 64-bit platforms).

questions.question: If int *ptr holds address 1000 on a system where sizeof(int) == 4, what address does ptr + 1 yield?
questions.explanation: Pointer addition steps by element byte size: 1000 + (1 	imes 4) = 1004.

questions.question: If char *cptr holds address 2000, what address does cptr + 3 evaluate to (sizeof(char) == 1)?
What arithmetic operation is valid between two pointers pointing elements within the same array?

options.A: Subtraction (ptr2 - ptr1), yielding element count distance between them

questions.explanation: Pointer subtraction yields the integer distance in elements between array elements.

questions.question: What happens if you attempt to add two pointers together ptr1 + ptr2 in C?

options.A: Compiler error (adding two pointers is illegal syntax)

questions.explanation: Adding two memory addresses is illegal in C.

questions.question: Given double *dp = 5000;, what address is computed by dp + 2 assuming sizeof(double) == 8?
What does decrementing a pointer ptr-- do?

options.A: Moves pointer address backward by sizeof(*ptr) bytes

questions.explanation: ptr-- steps pointer address down by one element type width.

questions.question: What relationship exists between an array identifier arr and a pointer in C?

options.A: Array identifier arr automatically decays into a constant pointer to its first element &arr[0] in expressions
options.B: Arrays and pointers are identical in every way

questions.explanation: An array name decays to address &arr[0] in most expressions.

questions.question: In pointer-array equivalence, how is array indexing arr[i] interpreted by the compiler?

options.A: *(arr + i)

questions.explanation: Subscript notation arr[i] is syntax sugar for dereferenced offset *(arr + i).

questions.question: Why is i[arr] valid C syntax identical to arr[i]?

options.A: Because i[arr] translates to *(i + arr), which equals *(arr + i) by commutative addition

questions.explanation: *(i + arr) equals *(arr + i) due to addition commutativity.

questions.question: What is a key difference between int arr[5]; and int *ptr;?

options.A: arr allocates 20 bytes of contiguous memory and arr address is non-assignable; ptr allocates pointer storage and can be reassigned to point elsewhere

questions.explanation: Arrays allocate element memory blocks; pointers hold memory addresses.

questions.question: Given int arr[] = {10, 20, 30}; int *p = arr;, what is *(p + 1)?
questions.explanation: p+1 points to arr[1] (20); *(p+1) dereferences it to yield 20.

questions.question: What is *p++ vs (*p)++ when p points to an integer array?

options.A: *p++ fetches current value then advances pointer p; (*p)++ increments the integer value in memory leaving pointer p unchanged

questions.explanation: Operator precedence binds *p++ to pointer address post-increment.

questions.question: How do you declare an array of 5 integer pointers in C?

options.A: int *arr[5];

questions.explanation: int *arr[5]; declares an array of 5 pointers to int.

questions.question: What does int (*arr)[5]; declare (notice parentheses around *arr)?

options.A: A pointer to a 1D array of 5 integers

questions.explanation: Parentheses bind *arr first, making arr a single pointer to an array of 5 ints.

questions.question: Where are arrays of character pointers char *names[] = {"Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"}; frequently used?

options.A: For managing collections of variable-length string literals efficiently without wasting padding space

questions.explanation: Pointer arrays hold direct pointers to strings of varying lengths.

questions.question: How many total pointers are contained inside char *argv[] parameter in main(int argc, char *argv[])?

options.A: argc pointers (plus a terminating NULL pointer)

questions.explanation: argv is an array of character pointers holding argc + 1 elements.

questions.question: How do you access the 2nd character of the 1st string in char *colors[] = {"Red", "Green"};?

options.A: colors[0][1] ('e' in "Red")

questions.explanation: colors[0] gets pointer to "Red"; colors[0][1] gets second char 'e'.

questions.question: What is memory layout advantage of char *str_arr[] over char str_arr[5][50]?

options.A: char* array allocates only exact bytes needed per string; 2D char array wastes unused column buffer bytes

questions.explanation: Ragged pointer arrays avoid fixed-width column memory waste.

questions.question: Which standard header file provides prototypes for dynamic memory functions malloc(), calloc(), realloc(), free()?

options.A: <stdlib.h>

questions.explanation: <stdlib.h> declares heap allocation routines.

questions.question: What region of memory is managed by dynamic memory functions (malloc/free)?

options.A: Heap memory

questions.explanation: Dynamic allocation requests memory from the heap.

questions.question: What is the key difference between malloc(n * sizeof(int)) and calloc(n, sizeof(int))?

options.A: malloc leaves allocated bytes uninitialized (garbage values); calloc zeroes all allocated memory bytes

questions.explanation: calloc initializes allocated memory bytes to zero.

questions.question: What value do malloc() and calloc() return if heap memory allocation fails?

options.A: NULL pointer

questions.explanation: Returns NULL when heap memory is exhausted.

questions.question: What happens if a program allocates heap memory repeatedly with malloc() but fails to release it using free()?

options.A: Memory leak, gradually consuming available system RAM

questions.explanation: Failing to free() unneeded heap memory creates memory leaks.

questions.question: What does realloc(ptr, new_size) do?

options.A: Resizes previously allocated heap block ptr to new_size, preserving existing contents up to minimum of old/new sizes

questions.explanation: realloc adjusts heap allocation block size.

unit: Unit 4: Unit 4: Functions and Program Organization

questions.question: What components constitute a complete C function definition?

options.A: Return type, function name, parameter list, and function body block {}

questions.explanation: A function definition specifies return type, identifier, parameters, and executable body.

questions.question: Which keyword specifies that a function returns no value to its caller?

options.A: void

questions.explanation: void indicates absence of return value or parameters.

questions.question: What happens when a function specified with return type int finishes without executing a return statement?

options.A: Returning without a value in a non-void function yields undefined behavior if caller uses return value

questions.explanation: Failing to return a value from a non-void function leads to undefined behavior if caller reads return value.

questions.question: Can a function in C return multiple values directly via a single return statement (e.g. return a, b;)?

options.A: No, a C return statement can evaluate and return at most a single value (comma operator evaluates to b only)

questions.explanation: return a, b; uses comma operator, returning only b. Multiple outputs require pointers or structures.

questions.question: Where in source code can functions be defined in standard C?

options.A: At file global scope (C does not permit nested function definitions inside other functions)

questions.explanation: Standard ISO C prohibits nested function definitions.

questions.question: What is the function body block?

options.A: Compound statement enclosed in {} containing local variable declarations and instructions

questions.explanation: The block inside {} executes when function is called.

questions.question: How is a function invoked or accessed in C source code?

options.A: By writing its name followed by argument list in parentheses func_name(arg1, arg2);

questions.explanation: Function access uses identifier followed by argument parentheses.

questions.question: What occurs during program control execution when a function call is executed?

options.A: Current execution pauses, control jumps to function entry point, executes body, then resumes caller at call site

questions.explanation: Function calls push stack frames and transfer control.

questions.question: What happens if a function argument type does not match the formal parameter type in a function call?

options.A: Implicit type conversion occurs if compatible; otherwise compiler warning/error occurs

questions.explanation: C performs implicit parameter conversions where standard type conversions exist.

questions.question: Can a function call statement be used as part of a larger mathematical expression, e.g. x = 5 + calculate(y);?

options.A: Yes, if the function returns a compatible value type
options.B: No, function calls must stand alone

questions.explanation: Valued function calls evaluate as expressions.

questions.question: What is returned when calling a function whose prototype is double square(double x)?

options.A: A double-precision floating-point value

questions.explanation: Return type specifies double.

questions.question: What happens to local variables created inside a function after function execution completes and returns?

options.A: Their stack memory frame is deallocated automatically

questions.explanation: Automatic stack variables pop on return.

questions.question: What is a function prototype (declaration) in C?

options.A: A statement declaring function return type, name, and parameter types before its definition/use

questions.explanation: Prototypes inform the compiler of function signature before invocation.

questions.question: Why are function prototypes recommended at the top of C source files or header files?

options.A: To enable compiler syntax checking of parameter count and argument types before function definition appears

questions.explanation: Prototypes enforce type checking and allow function usage before definition.

questions.question: Which declaration represents a valid function prototype?

options.A: int add(int a, int b); or int add(int, int);
options.D: function int add(int a, int b);

questions.explanation: Prototype specifies return type, name, parameter types, ending with semicolon.

questions.question: What happens in older C if a function is called without a prior prototype or definition?

options.A: Implicit function declaration assumes return type int (deprecated/removed in modern C standards)

questions.explanation: Implicit int functions were allowed in C89 but prohibited in C99/C11.

questions.question: What does a function prototype void process(void); communicate to compiler?

options.A: Function accepts zero parameters and returns no value

questions.explanation: void parameter explicitly forbids arguments.

questions.question: What is the difference between a function prototype and a function definition?

options.A: Prototype specifies signature ending in ;; definition provides actual function body enclosed in {}

questions.explanation: Prototype declares signature; definition provides body.

questions.question: What is the memory structure used by runtime systems to manage function call frames, parameters, and return addresses?

options.A: Call Stack (Stack frames)

questions.explanation: Call stack frames push on call and pop on return.

questions.question: What risk occurs if functions call each other infinitely without a termination condition?

options.A: Stack Overflow (exhausting stack space)

questions.explanation: Infinite recursion/calls exhaust stack memory bounds.

questions.question: What are actual arguments vs formal parameters?

options.A: Actual arguments are values passed in the call site; formal parameters are variables declared in function signature

questions.explanation: Actual arguments evaluate at call site into formal parameter storage.

questions.question: In C, what order are function call arguments evaluated prior to passing?

options.A: Unspecified by C standard (compiler-dependent evaluation order)

questions.explanation: C standard leaves parameter evaluation order unspecified.

questions.question: What is an inline function (inline keyword introduced in C99)?

options.A: Suggests compiler replace function call with inline expansion of body code to eliminate call overhead
options.B: Forces function to run on GPU

questions.explanation: inline hints compiler to expand code directly at call site.

questions.question: What is a function pointer in C?

options.A: A pointer variable holding the memory address of executable function code

questions.explanation: Function pointers store executable code addresses.

questions.question: What default parameter passing mechanism is employed by C for all non-array scalar variables?

options.A: Pass by Value

questions.explanation: C passes scalar arguments strictly by value (copying data).

questions.question: In Pass by Value, if a function modifies its formal parameter variable inside the function body, what happens to the caller's variable?

options.A: Caller variable remains completely unchanged because function worked on a copy

questions.explanation: Changes to value copies do not affect caller variables.

questions.question: How is 'Pass by Reference' simulated in C when a function needs to modify caller variables directly?

options.A: By passing memory pointers (&var) as arguments and dereferencing them inside function (*ptr)

questions.explanation: Passing addresses permits functions to modify caller memory.

questions.question: To write a swap function void swap(int *a, int *b) that swaps caller variables x=5, y=10, how must it be called?

options.A: swap(&x, &y);

questions.explanation: Addresses &x and &y must be passed to pointer parameters.

questions.question: Why do arrays automatically behave as if passed by reference when passed to functions?

options.A: Array names automatically decay to pointers to their first element &arr[0]
options.C: Arrays are stored in global RAM

questions.explanation: Array decay passes pointer address to function.

questions.question: What performance advantage does passing a large struct by pointer (const StructType *ptr) offer over passing by value?

options.A: Avoids expensive copying of all struct member bytes onto stack frame

questions.explanation: Passing pointer copies 8 bytes instead of entire structure body.

questions.question: What is a recursive function in C?

options.A: A function that calls itself directly or indirectly
options.B: A function with no return type

questions.explanation: Recursion occurs when a function invokes itself.

questions.question: What essential component must every valid recursive function possess to avoid infinite execution?

options.A: Base Case (termination condition that returns without recursive call)

questions.explanation: Base cases stop recursive call chain.

questions.question: What happens if a recursive function lacks a valid base case?

options.A: Infinite recursion resulting in stack overflow crash

questions.explanation: Exhausting stack frames triggers stack overflow.

questions.question: In computing factorial N! recursively long fact(int n) { if (n <= 1) return 1; else return n * fact(n - 1); }, what is the base case?
questions.explanation: n <= 1 returns 1 directly without further recursive calls.

questions.question: What is 'Tail Recursion'?

options.A: A recursive call occurring as the absolute final statement of a function, allowing tail-call optimization

questions.explanation: Tail recursion enables compilers to reuse call stack frames.

questions.question: Compared to iterative loops, what is a potential drawback of recursion?

options.A: Higher function call stack overhead and risk of stack overflow

questions.explanation: Each call incurs stack allocation overhead.

questions.question: Which four storage class specifiers exist in standard C?

options.A: auto, register, static, extern

questions.explanation: C defines storage classes auto, register, static, extern.

questions.question: What is the default storage class for local variables declared inside a block?

options.A: auto

questions.explanation: Local variables default to automatic (auto) storage.

questions.question: What does the register storage class hint to the compiler?

options.A: Suggests storing variable in CPU register for fast access instead of RAM

questions.explanation: register hints CPU register storage.

questions.question: Is the address-of operator & permitted on a variable declared with register specifier in C?

options.A: No, taking address & of a register variable is illegal in C even if compiler placed it in RAM

questions.explanation: C standard explicitly forbids & on register variables.

questions.question: What does the extern keyword specify?

options.A: Declares a global variable/function defined in another source file or module without allocating new storage

questions.explanation: extern references global symbols across translation units.

questions.question: Where are static and global variables stored in memory?

options.A: Data segment / BSS segment (initialized/uninitialized data segment)

questions.explanation: Global and static variables reside in static data segments throughout program lifetime.

questions.question: What does 'Scope' of a variable mean in C?

options.A: The region of source code where a variable identifier is visible and accessible

questions.explanation: Scope governs identifier visibility.

questions.question: What does 'Lifetime' of a variable specify?

options.A: The period of time during runtime execution that a variable retains allocated memory storage

questions.explanation: Lifetime defines allocation duration.

questions.question: What is block scope (local scope)?

options.A: Variable is accessible only within the enclosing {} block where it is declared
options.B: Variable is accessible everywhere in program

questions.explanation: Block scope limits visibility to enclosing {}.

questions.question: What is file scope (global scope)?

options.A: Variable declared outside all functions, accessible from declaration to end of translation unit

questions.explanation: File scope variables exist outside functions.

questions.question: What happens if a local block variable shares the identical name as a global variable?

options.A: Local variable shadows (hides) the global variable within the local block scope

questions.explanation: Inner declarations shadow outer scope identifiers.

questions.question: What is the lifetime of a local auto variable vs a local static variable?

options.A: auto lifetime lasts during function block execution; static lifetime spans entire program run

questions.explanation: auto destroys on exit; static persists across calls.

questions.question: What happens when a local variable inside a function is declared with static int count = 0;?

options.A: It is initialized once, and retains its modified value across multiple calls to that function
options.B: It resets to 0 on every function call

questions.explanation: Local static variables maintain state between function calls.

questions.question: If an global variable or function is declared with static at file scope (static int hidden;), what effect does it have?

options.A: Restricts visibility/linkage strictly to the current source file (internal linkage)
options.B: Makes it accessible across all files

questions.explanation: File-scope static restricts linkage to current translation unit.

questions.question: What default initial value do uninitialized static variables automatically receive?

options.A: Zero (0 / NULL)

questions.explanation: static memory in BSS segment is zeroed automatically.

questions.question: When is the initialization expression of a static variable evaluated?

options.A: Once at program startup before main() begins

questions.explanation: Static initializers run at startup phase.

questions.question: Given void counter() { static int c = 5; c++; printf("%d ", c); }, what prints after 3 sequential calls?
questions.explanation: Call 1: c becomes 6; Call 2: c becomes 7; Call 3: c becomes 8.

questions.question: Can a static variable initializer expression contain runtime non-constant function calls like static int x = getValue(); in C?

options.A: No, C requires static initializers to be compile-time constant expressions

questions.explanation: C standard mandates compile-time constants for static initializers.

questions.question: What defines a global variable in C?

options.A: Variable declared outside all functions, accessible across the program source

questions.explanation: Global variables sit outside function scope.

questions.question: What default initial value do uninitialized global variables receive?

options.A: Zero (0)

questions.explanation: Global variables zero-initialize by default.

questions.question: Why is excessive reliance on global variables discouraged in software architecture?

options.A: Makes state tracking difficult, creates hidden dependencies, and causes side-effect bugs across functions

questions.explanation: Global state harms modularity and concurrency.

questions.question: How can file A access a global variable int score = 100; defined in file B?

options.A: By placing extern int score; declaration in file A
options.B: By re-declaring int score = 100; in file A

questions.explanation: extern imports global declarations across modules.

questions.question: What lifetime do global variables possess?

options.A: Program lifetime (allocated at program launch, destroyed at exit)

questions.explanation: Global variables persist throughout execution.

questions.question: What happens if two source files define the identical global variable int total = 0; without static or extern?

options.A: Linker error (duplicate symbol / multiple definition)

questions.explanation: Multiple definitions of strong symbols trigger linker collision.

questions.question: What is a struct in C?

options.A: User-defined composite data type grouping variables of potentially different types under a single name
options.B: An array of same data types

questions.explanation: Structures aggregate heterogeneous data members.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a structure type in C?

options.A: struct

questions.explanation: struct defines structure types.

questions.question: Which syntax correctly defines a structure named Student?

options.A: struct Student { int id; char name[20]; float gpa; };
options.B: struct Student { int id, char name[20] };

questions.explanation: Standard syntax ends with a semicolon after closing brace };.

questions.question: Why is a terminating semicolon ; mandatory after a struct declaration closing brace };?

options.A: Completes the type declaration statement (allowing variable instances to follow if desired)

questions.explanation: The semicolon terminates the structure declaration statement.

questions.question: Does declaring a structure definition struct Point { int x; int y; }; allocate memory by itself?

options.A: No, it defines a type schema; memory is allocated only when variables of that struct type are instantiated

questions.explanation: Type definitions create schemas; instantiation allocates storage.

questions.question: What is structure padding in C?

options.A: Unused alignment bytes inserted by compiler between struct members to align data on word memory boundaries

questions.explanation: Compilers insert padding bytes to enforce CPU memory alignment rules.

questions.question: Which operator is used to access a member of a structure variable directly?

options.A: Direct member selection operator . (Dot operator)

questions.explanation: Dot operator . accesses struct members from struct variables.
