questions.question: Given struct Point { int x; int y; } p1;, how do you assign 15 to member x?
questions.explanation: p1.x accesses member x.

questions.question: Can you assign one structure variable directly to another of the identical type (p2 = p1;)?

options.A: Yes, performs a bitwise/memberwise copy of all structure data fields

questions.explanation: Structure assignment performs complete memberwise copying.

questions.question: How can a structure variable be initialized upon declaration?

options.A: struct Point p = {10, 20};

questions.explanation: Curly braces {} initialize struct fields sequentially.

questions.question: Does the relational equality comparison if (p1 == p2) work directly on whole structure variables in standard C?

options.A: No, C does not support direct == comparison on structures; members must be compared individually (or via memcmp)

questions.explanation: C forbids == on structures due to potential padding byte garbage.

questions.question: What C99 feature allows initializing struct members by name struct Point p = {.y = 5, .x = 10};?

options.A: Designated Initializers

questions.explanation: Designated initializers map explicitly to field names.

questions.question: How do you declare an array capable of storing 100 struct Student instances?

options.A: struct Student class_list[100];

questions.explanation: Array of structures uses standard array declaration syntax.

questions.question: How do you access the gpa member of the 5th student in struct Student class_list[100];?

options.A: class_list[4].gpa

questions.explanation: class_list[4] selects 5th array element; .gpa selects member field.

questions.question: How are elements of an array of structures laid out in physical memory?

options.A: Contiguously in a single sequential block of memory

questions.explanation: Array elements lie sequentially in memory.

questions.question: How is an array of structures initialized inline?

options.A: struct Point pts[2] = { {1, 2}, {3, 4} };

questions.explanation: Nested curly brace sets initialize array elements.

questions.question: What is the total byte size of struct Item items[10]; if sizeof(struct Item) == 32?

options.A: 320 bytes (10 	imes 32)

questions.explanation: Total memory size = count 	imes element byte size = 10 	imes 32 = 320.

questions.question: How do you loop through and print all items in an array of structures?

options.A: for(int i=0; i<N; i++) printf("%d", items[i].id);

questions.explanation: Index loop iterates array accessing items[i].id.

questions.question: What is a nested structure in C?

options.A: A structure that includes an instance of another structure as one of its member fields

questions.explanation: Nested structures embed struct types within struct fields.

questions.question: Given struct Date { int day, month, year; }; struct Emp { char name[20]; struct Date doj; }; struct Emp e;, how do you access joining year?

options.A: e.doj.year

questions.explanation: Chained dot operators access nested struct members.

questions.question: Can a structure contain an instance of itself directly as a non-pointer member field (struct Node { int data; struct Node next; };)?

options.A: No, causes infinite size recursion compile error (must use a pointer struct Node *next;)

questions.explanation: Embedding complete instance of self requires infinite memory size; pointer is required.

questions.question: How do you initialize a nested structure variable inline?

options.A: struct Emp e = {"John", {15, 8, 2023}};

questions.explanation: Inner braces initialize nested structure member fields.

questions.question: What is an anonymous nested struct (introduced in C11)?

options.A: A structure member defined without a member field identifier name, making its members accessible directly in parent

questions.explanation: Anonymous structs expose fields directly into parent scope.

questions.question: If struct A contains struct B, what is sizeof(struct A) relative to sizeof(struct B)?

options.A: sizeof(struct A) is at least sizeof(struct B) plus bytes of other members and padding

questions.explanation: Parent struct memory includes nested struct size.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the typedef keyword in C?

options.A: Creates a user-defined type alias name for an existing data type

questions.explanation: typedef establishes descriptive type aliases.

questions.question: Which syntax correctly defines ulong as an alias for unsigned long int?

options.A: typedef unsigned long int ulong;

questions.explanation: typedef original_type alias_name;.

questions.question: How does typedef simplify structure variable declarations?

options.A: Eliminates requirement to write struct keyword repeatedly when declaring variables

questions.explanation: typedef struct Point Point; allows writing Point p; instead of struct Point p;.

questions.question: What is the difference between #define macro alias and typedef type alias?

options.A: typedef is parsed and scope-checked by compiler; #define is preprocessor textual replacement

questions.explanation: typedef is handled by compiler's type system.

questions.question: How do you combine structure definition and typedef in a single statement?

options.A: typedef struct { int x, y; } Point;
options.B: struct typedef Point { int x, y; };
options.C: typedef Point = struct { int x, y; };
options.D: type struct Point { int x, y; };

questions.explanation: Combines struct declaration with alias Point.

questions.question: Does typedef create a genuinely brand-new hardware data type?

options.A: No, it creates a new synonym/alias for an existing type
options.B: Yes, creates new CPU machine type

questions.explanation: typedef only establishes an alias name.

questions.question: What happens when a structure is passed by value to a function void display(struct Student s)?

options.A: A complete copy of all member fields is pushed onto the stack call frame

questions.explanation: Passing struct by value duplicates all member bytes.

questions.question: Why is passing structures by pointer void modify(struct Student *s) preferred for large structures?

options.A: Avoids memory copy overhead and permits function to modify original struct members

questions.explanation: Pointer passing saves stack copying and enables caller updates.

questions.question: Can a C function return an entire structure variable by value (struct Point create_point(int x, int y))?

options.A: Yes, C functions can return complete structure values

questions.explanation: C supports returning complete structure instances.

questions.question: If a function receives const struct Data *d, what does const protect?

options.A: Prevents function from modifying structure member fields through pointer d

questions.explanation: const enforces read-only access to structure fields.

questions.question: How do you call a function expecting a structure pointer void process(struct Data *p) using variable struct Data d?

options.A: process(&d);

questions.explanation: Pass address &d to structure pointer parameter.

questions.question: What is a factory function pattern in structure management?

options.A: A function that constructs, initializes, and returns a new structure instance (or pointer to heap struct)

questions.explanation: Factory functions encapsulate creation and initialization.

questions.question: Which operator is used to access structure members through a structure pointer variable struct Point *ptr;?

options.A: Arrow operator -> (Indirect member selection)

questions.explanation: ptr->member accesses members via pointer.

questions.question: How is the arrow operator ptr->x equivalently written using dereference * and dot . operators?

options.A: (*ptr).x

questions.explanation: (*ptr).x dereferences pointer first, then accesses member.

questions.question: Why are parentheses mandatory in (*ptr).x when replacing ptr->x?

options.A: Because dot operator . has higher precedence than dereference operator * (*ptr.x would parse as *(ptr.x))

questions.explanation: Dot . operator binds tighter than dereference *.

questions.question: How do you dynamically allocate memory for a structure variable on the heap?

options.A: struct Point *p = malloc(sizeof(struct Point));

questions.explanation: malloc(sizeof(struct Point)) allocates necessary heap bytes.

questions.question: What must be done after finishing work with dynamically allocated structure pointer p?

options.A: free(p); to release heap memory and avoid memory leaks

questions.explanation: free(p) releases allocated heap memory.

questions.question: Given struct Student { char name[20]; }; struct Student *ptr = malloc(sizeof(struct Student));, how do you copy "Bob" into name?

options.A: strcpy(ptr->name, "Bob");

questions.explanation: strcpy copies string bytes into member array.

questions.question: What is a self-referential structure in C?

options.A: A structure containing a pointer member that points to an instance of the same structure type
options.B: A structure containing itself as a value member

questions.explanation: Self-referential structs hold pointers to their own struct type.

questions.question: Where are self-referential structures fundamentally employed in computer science?

options.A: Building dynamic data structures like Linked Lists, Trees, Graphs, Stacks, and Queues

questions.explanation: Pointers to self enable linked nodes in lists/trees.

questions.question: Which code snippet correctly declares a singly linked list node?

options.A: struct Node { int data; struct Node *next; };
options.B: struct Node { int data; struct Node next; };
options.D: typedef struct { int data; Node next; } Node;

questions.explanation: struct Node *next; is a pointer to same structure type.

questions.question: What value indicates the end of a singly linked list chain in the next pointer of the final tail node?

options.A: NULL

questions.explanation: NULL designates terminal node list end.

questions.question: How many self-referential pointer members are contained in a doubly linked list node?

options.A: Two pointers (struct Node *prev; struct Node *next;)

questions.explanation: Doubly linked nodes maintain prev and next pointers.

questions.question: How many child pointer members exist in a binary tree node self-referential structure?

options.A: Two pointers (struct TreeNode *left; struct TreeNode *right;)

questions.explanation: Binary tree nodes hold left and right child pointers.

questions.question: What is a union in C?

options.A: User-defined data type where all member fields share the exact same starting memory location
options.B: A struct where every member has separate memory

questions.explanation: Unions overlay member fields in shared memory space.

questions.question: How is the total memory size of a union calculated by the compiler?

options.A: Equal to the byte size of its largest member field (plus alignment padding)
options.B: Sum of sizes of all members

questions.explanation: Union size accommodates its single largest member field.

questions.question: What happens when you write to one member u.i = 100; and then write to another member u.f = 3.14f; in a union?

options.A: The write to u.f overwrites the shared memory space, corrupting/replacing the value stored in u.i

questions.explanation: Unions hold only one active member value at a time.

questions.question: Which keyword defines a union in C?

options.A: union

questions.explanation: union defines shared memory composite types.

questions.question: Where are unions practically utilized in system programming?

options.A: Saving memory in variant type structures, hardware register bit-level access, and protocol packet parsing

questions.explanation: Unions optimize storage for mutually exclusive data variants.

questions.question: Given union Data { int i; char c; double d; } u;, what is sizeof(u) assuming sizeof(int)==4, sizeof(char)==1, sizeof(double)==8?

options.A: 8 bytes (size of largest member double)

questions.explanation: Size matches largest member double (8 bytes).

questions.question: Why is secondary storage file handling required in C applications?

options.A: RAM data is volatile and lost when the program exits; files provide non-volatile persistent storage on disk
options.B: RAM is too small for loop variables
options.C: Required by C compilers to store integers

questions.explanation: Files preserve data across program terminations.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Text files and Binary files in disk storage?

options.A: Text files store data as human-readable ASCII/UTF characters with line endings; binary files store raw bytes mirroring RAM data
options.D: Text files require special GPU hardware

questions.explanation: Text files hold character encodings; binary files hold raw byte streams.

questions.question: What object type in <stdio.h> represents an active file stream in C programs?

options.A: FILE* (Pointer to FILE structure)

questions.explanation: FILE* manages file stream buffer state and position pointers.

questions.question: Which three standard file streams are automatically opened when a C program starts execution?

options.A: stdin (Standard Input), stdout (Standard Output), stderr (Standard Error)

questions.explanation: stdin, stdout, stderr open automatically on startup.

questions.question: What advantage does file storage offer for large datasets over keyboard input?

options.A: Enables automated bulk data processing, repeatability, and persistent auditing without manual typing

questions.explanation: Files allow automated batch reading and writing.

questions.question: What happens to data stored strictly inside local variables when a program terminates without writing to a file?

subtopics.title: 5.2 Opening and Closing a Data File

questions.question: Which C standard library function opens a file stream?

options.A: fopen("filename", "mode")

questions.explanation: fopen opens file streams with specified access mode.

questions.question: What mode string opens a text file strictly for reading, returning NULL if file does not exist?
questions.explanation: "r" mode opens existing files for reading.

questions.question: What occurs when opening a file with write mode "w" if the target file already exists on disk?

options.A: Existing file content is completely erased (truncated to 0 bytes)

questions.explanation: "w" mode truncates existing files to 0 length.

questions.question: Which access mode string appends new data to the end of an existing file without erasing prior content?

questions.question: What value does fopen() return if the requested file cannot be opened (e.g. file missing or permission denied)?

options.A: NULL

questions.explanation: fopen yields NULL on stream open failure.

questions.question: Which function closes an open file stream and flushes unwritten stream buffers to disk?

questions.question: Which functions write and read a single character to/from a file stream fp?

options.A: fputc(ch, fp) and fgetc(fp)

questions.explanation: fputc and fgetc perform character file I/O.

questions.question: Which function writes formatted output to a file stream identically to printf()?

options.A: fprintf(fp, "format", args...)

questions.explanation: fprintf writes formatted text into file streams.

questions.question: Which function reads formatted input from a file stream identically to scanf()?

options.A: fscanf(fp, "format", &args...)

questions.explanation: fscanf parses formatted input from stream.

questions.question: Which pair of functions performs raw binary block reading and writing for structures/arrays?

options.A: fread() and fwrite()

questions.explanation: fread and fwrite handle raw binary buffer blocks.

questions.question: What parameter list signature does fwrite() take?

options.A: fwrite(const void *ptr, size_t size, size_t nmemb, FILE *stream)

questions.question: What function tests if the End-Of-File indicator has been set for stream fp?

questions.question: Which function sets the file position indicator to a specific byte offset in stream fp?

options.A: fseek(fp, offset, whence)

questions.question: What do the whence constants SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR, and SEEK_END signify in fseek()?

options.A: SEEK_SET = File beginning; SEEK_CUR = Current file position; SEEK_END = End of file

questions.question: Which function returns the current byte position offset of stream fp relative to file start?

options.A: ftell(fp)

questions.explanation: ftell yields current byte offset position.

questions.question: What does rewind(fp) do to file stream fp?

questions.explanation: rewind resets file offset position to 0.

questions.question: How can fseek() and ftell() be combined to calculate total byte size of file fp?

options.A: fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END); long size = ftell(fp);

questions.question: What is random access file processing vs sequential processing?

questions.explanation: fseek grants direct random offset access.

questions.question: What does the register keyword ask the compiler to do with a variable declaration?

options.A: Request storing the variable inside a CPU register for high-speed access

questions.explanation: register requests hardware CPU register storage.

questions.question: Why is taking the address of a register variable &reg_var prohibited in C?

options.A: CPU registers reside in CPU processor core and do not possess standard RAM memory addresses

questions.question: Is the compiler obligated to grant a register request in modern C?

questions.question: Which data types are suitable for register storage hints?

questions.explanation: Registers store small word-sized integers/pointers.

questions.question: Where can register storage class declarations exist?

options.A: Strictly as local variables inside function/block scope or formal parameters

questions.explanation: register applies only to automatic local scope variables.

questions.question: What happens in C11 standard regarding register keyword usage?

options.A: Retained for backward compatibility, though modern compilers perform register allocation automatically via optimization passes

questions.question: Which declaration syntax creates a bit field member status holding 3 bits inside a struct?

options.A: unsigned int status : 3;

questions.explanation: Colon syntax : num_bits designates bit field size.

questions.question: What maximum unsigned integer value can be stored in a 3-bit bit field (unsigned int b : 3)?
questions.explanation: 3 unsigned bits represent values 0 through 7.

questions.question: Can you apply the address-of operator & to a bit field member of a structure (&obj.bitfield)?

options.A: No, bit fields may not start on byte boundaries, so taking address & of a bit field is prohibited in C

questions.explanation: C standard prohibits taking address & of bit fields.

questions.question: Where are bit fields predominantly utilized?

options.A: Hardware device driver register mapping, memory-constrained embedded systems, and network headers

questions.explanation: Bit fields map hardware registers and pack flags.

questions.question: What does an unnamed bit field with width 0 (unsigned int : 0;) perform inside a struct?

options.A: Forces alignment of the next bit field to the boundary of the next storage unit type

questions.explanation: Zero-width unnamed bit fields force boundary alignment.

questions.question: What is an enum (enumeration) in C?

options.A: A user-defined data type consisting of named integer constants

questions.explanation: Enumerations define symbolic integer constants.

questions.question: Which keyword creates an enumeration in C?

options.A: enum

questions.explanation: enum declares enumeration types.

questions.question: By default, what integer values are assigned to names in enum Day { SUN, MON, TUE };?

options.A: SUN = 0, MON = 1, TUE = 2

questions.explanation: Enums auto-increment starting from 0.

questions.question: If defined as enum Status { OK = 200, ERROR = 500, TIMEOUT };, what integer value is assigned to TIMEOUT?

options.A: 501 (increments preceding explicit value by 1)

questions.explanation: Unassigned enum values increment previous explicitly assigned constant by 1.

questions.question: What readability advantage do enumerations offer over raw magic numbers?

options.A: Replaces obscure numerical constants with meaningful descriptive identifiers in source code

questions.explanation: Enums make code self-documenting and maintainable.

questions.question: What is the underlying data type used by compilers to store enum values?

options.A: Compatible integer type (usually int)

questions.explanation: Enumeration constants are treated as integer types.

questions.question: What are the standard parameter signatures passed to main() for handling command line arguments?

options.A: int main(int argc, char *argv[])

questions.explanation: argc holds parameter count; argv holds array of parameter string pointers.

questions.question: What does parameter argc represent in command line execution?

options.A: Argument Count (total number of command line arguments passed, including program executable name)

questions.explanation: argc counts total command line argument tokens.

questions.question: What is stored inside argv[0]?

options.A: The program name/path invoked on command line

questions.explanation: argv[0] contains program invocation path.

questions.question: If a program is launched as ./myprog data.txt 100, what are the values of argc, argv[1], and argv[2]?

options.A: argc = 3, argv[1] = "data.txt", argv[2] = "100"

questions.explanation: 3 tokens: myprog (0), data.txt (1), 100 (2).

questions.question: How do you convert numeric command line string argument argv[2] into an integer inside main()?

options.A: int num = atoi(argv[2]); or strtol()

questions.explanation: atoi / strtol converts string representation to numeric int.

questions.question: What value is guaranteed for argv[argc] according to C standard?

options.A: NULL pointer

questions.explanation: argv[argc] is explicitly defined as NULL pointer.

questions.question: Which standard function in <stdlib.h> performs quicksort sorting on arbitrary arrays?

options.A: qsort(base, num, size, comparator)

questions.explanation: qsort performs in-place sorting using a user comparator function.

questions.question: Which function in <stdlib.h> performs binary search on a sorted array?

options.A: bsearch(key, base, num, size, comparator)

questions.explanation: bsearch performs binary search on sorted elements.

questions.question: Which function declared in <string.h> sets N bytes of memory block to a specified byte value?

options.A: memset(ptr, value, num_bytes)

questions.explanation: memset fills memory bytes with constant value.

questions.question: Which function declared in <string.h> copies N bytes from source memory buffer to destination buffer?

options.A: memcpy(dest, src, num_bytes)

questions.explanation: memcpy copies non-overlapping raw memory bytes.

questions.question: What distinguishes memmove() from memcpy() when copying memory blocks?

options.A: memmove() handles overlapping source and destination memory buffers safely; memcpy() requires non-overlapping buffers

questions.explanation: memmove handles overlapping buffers safely.

questions.question: Which function in <time.h> returns current calendar time epoch timestamp?

options.A: time(NULL)

questions.explanation: time(NULL) returns seconds since Unix epoch.

questions.question: How is a macro defined using C preprocessor directives?

options.A: #define MACRO_NAME value

questions.explanation: #define sets preprocessor substitution macros.

questions.question: What is a parameterized (function-like) macro in C?

options.A: #define SQUARE(x) ((x) * (x))

questions.explanation: Function-like macros take arguments replaced textually.

questions.question: Why should macro parameter arguments always be enclosed in parentheses inside definition, e.g. #define MULT(a,b) ((a) * (b))?

options.A: To prevent operator precedence bugs when complex expressions are passed as arguments

questions.explanation: Parentheses preserve evaluation precedence during text substitution.

questions.question: What operator in macro definitions turns a macro parameter into a string literal (#x)?

options.A: Stringizing operator #
options.D: Escape operator Answer: A Explanation: Single # stringizes macro arguments.

questions.question: What operator in macro definitions merges two tokens into a single identifier (a ## b)?

options.A: Token pasting operator ##

questions.explanation: ## pastes tokens together.

questions.question: What side-effect pitfall occurs in SQUARE(x++) when defined as #define SQUARE(a) ((a) * (a))?

options.A: x++ evaluates twice, resulting in double increment and unintended results

questions.explanation: Macros evaluate argument expressions multiple times.

questions.question: When does the preprocessor execute in the compilation pipeline?

options.A: Before actual syntax compilation begins (transforms source text)

questions.explanation: The preprocessor operates before parsing and compilation.

questions.question: What is the difference between #include <file.h> and #include "file.h"?

options.A: <file.h> searches standard system library header paths; "file.h" searches local project directory first

questions.explanation: Angle brackets search system headers; quotes search user project files first.

questions.question: Which preprocessor directives perform conditional compilation?

options.A: #ifdef, #ifndef, #if, #else, #elif, #endif

questions.explanation: Conditional preprocessor directives include/exclude source blocks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of header guards (#ifndef HEADER_H #define HEADER_H ... #endif)?

options.A: Prevents duplicate header inclusion and symbol redefinition compile errors

questions.explanation: Header guards prevent double inclusion.

questions.question: What directive undefines a previously defined macro?

options.A: #undef MACRO_NAME

questions.explanation: #undef cancels preprocessor macro definition.

questions.question: Which predefined macro holds current source line number and file name during preprocessor pass?

options.A: __LINE__ and __FILE__

questions.explanation: __LINE__ and __FILE__ expand to current file and line.

subtopics.title: 5.13 Brief overview of the differences standards of C Language

questions.question: What major evolution occurred moving from K&R C to ANSI C (C89)?

options.A: Addition of mandatory function prototypes, standard library standardization, const and volatile keywords

questions.explanation: C89 introduced prototypes, standard libraries, and qualifiers.

questions.question: Which features distinctly separate C99 from C89?

options.A: // comments, inline functions, variable declarations anywhere in block, long long int, variable length arrays

questions.explanation: C99 introduced modern scripting-friendly features like mixed declarations and // comments.

questions.question: What core features set C11 apart from C99?

options.A: Native multithreading <threads.h>, atomics <stdatomic.h>, anonymous structs, static assertions _Static_assert, _Generic expressions

questions.explanation: C11 focused on concurrency, atomic operations, and type generics.

questions.question: What distinguishes C17/C18 from C11?

options.A: Bug fixes and technical clarifications; introduced no new language syntax features

questions.explanation: C17 was purely a defect-fix maintenance revision.

questions.question: What key modern features are being introduced in C23?

options.A: nullptr constant keyword, auto type inference, #embed directive, constexpr, binary literals 0b

questions.explanation: C23 adds nullptr, auto type inference, #embed, and binary literals.

questions.question: Why is knowledge of C standards differences essential for C developers?

options.A: Ensures compiler flag selection (-std=c99, -std=c11), cross-compiler portability, and avoiding non-standard features

questions.explanation: Standard flags determine supported syntax features across toolchains.
